commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

decodeBlock() resized the tag buffer to the atom size before calling
tagDecoder(), but none of the decoders that receive that buffer write
more than the four tag bytes into it, so the resize was dead weight.

Also right-size the buffer in NikonTagsDecoder(): the sanity check
there rejects any payload that is not strictly smaller than the
buffer, so payload plus nul terminator never needs more bytes than
the buffer itself and the extra byte in the 201-byte allocation was
never used.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Nul-terminate strings

Go over the places where a DataBuf is treated as a C string and make
each nul terminator explicit, so that every buffer handed to
toString() or streamed as char* carries its own terminator instead of
depending on an earlier read or memset having left a zero byte in the
right place. Buffers that only hold four character codes are sized
for the terminator instead of relying on slack, and the oversized
ones are trimmed to what the fields actually need.

Also spell out the limit the Nikon NCTG sanity check enforces. It is
written against the buffer size, but what it stands for is the 200
byte limit of these payloads, which is what the error message right
below it already reports. State that number directly so the check
reads as the format limit it is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect lives in QuickTimeVideo::NikonTagsDecoder() (src/quicktimevideo.cpp) and only exists as the INTERACTION of the two edited commits; neither diff is faulty on its own and the bug is unreachable from either edit alone (verified empirically: each single-edit tree runs the PoC cleanly, only the combined tree aborts).

Commit 8aa4339068948e2c5495f7930b3c3e5bbab209de ('Remove unnecessary resize', first in history order) right-sizes the NCTG payload buffer from DataBuf buf(201) to DataBuf buf(200). This is provably safe at that point in history because the surrounding sanity check is still capacity-relative: 'if (dataLength >= buf.size())' rejects any payload not strictly smaller than the buffer, so payload plus the '\0' terminator never needs more than buf.size() bytes; 200 is exactly enough and the old 201 wasted one byte. Every other branch of the decoder reads at most 196 bytes, so nothing else depends on the lost byte.

Commit af80d515237dfc07073eb97931be4ed33e1aec3a ('Nul-terminate strings', second in history order) replaces that capacity-relative check with the documented format limit as a literal: 'if (dataLength >= buf.size())' becomes 'if (dataLength > 200)'. With the buffer still at its original 201 bytes this is a semantics-preserving refactor (both forms reject exactly dataLength >= 201), which is why the edit is invisible when read alone - and thematically it belongs to a commit whose whole topic is the nul terminator that this check guards.

Composed, the two commits disagree about what '200' means: the check now admits a payload of exactly 200 bytes into a buffer of exactly 200 bytes, and the terminator write 'buf.data()[dataLength] = \0'' then lands one byte past the end of the heap allocation (a 1-byte out-of-bounds WRITE, CWE-787, reached from the public API via ImageFactory::open() + readMetadata() on an in-contract QuickTime file whose udta/NCTG list declares a 200-byte ASCII payload).

A correct fix has to reconcile the two commits rather than patch one symptom: restoring the buffer to 201 bytes (touching only commit 8aa4339) hides the bug but leaves the check permanently decoupled from capacity, so any later resize re-opens it; changing the literal to 199 or '>=' (touching only commit af80d51) silently rejects a legal 200-byte payload and still leaves the check ignorant of the buffer size. The real repair is to make the check capacity-relative again AND keep the terminator in mind when sizing (e.g. dataLength + 1 <= buf.size() with buf sized accordingly), which requires reasoning about both commits - the contract between the sanity check and the buffer allocation - rather than about either diff in isolation. Each commit, read on its own, is correct maintenance: the first is a dead-code removal plus an exactly-sufficient right-sizing, the second is an explicit-terminator cleanup plus a no-op literalization of a check, and the intermediate trees (original, only-first-edit, only-second-edit) are all memory-safe on the proof-of-concept input.

pocs.entry_point: Exiv2::ImageFactory::open(const byte*, size_t) followed by Image::readMetadata() (QuickTime parser: decodeBlock -> tagDecoder -> userDataDecoder -> NikonTagsDecoder)
